title: Prefill Twice, Decode Once: Exploiting KV Cache Redundancy in Prompt Repetition

contributions.purpose: Establish that the first-copy KV cache in prompt repetition can be discarded at decode time without losing accuracy.
contributions.mechanism: Observe that during prefill the second copy's representations attend fully to the first copy and thus encode all necessary information, making the first-copy KV cache decode-time redundant.
contributions.evaluation: Validated indirectly by the downstream accuracy retention results (100%+ retention) and sanity checks (max abs diff = 0.0 for sliced KV, 100% first-token agreement).
contributions.source_quote: We identify that the first-copy KV cache in prompt repetition is decode-time redundant, enabling significant memory savings without accuracy loss.

contributions.purpose: Achieve the accuracy benefit of prompt repetition while halving decode-time KV cache memory.
contributions.mechanism: Propose PTDO (Prefill Twice, Decode Once): prefill P||P to build the full KV cache, slice to retain only the second-copy KV entries (positions |P| to 2|P|-1), then decode with correct RoPE position offsets (first generated token at position 2|P|). Training-free, no model modification.
contributions.evaluation: Presented as a training-free three-stage method; validated by ~50% KV cache reduction (KV ratio 0.506-0.595) at matched accuracy.
contributions.domain: LLM inference / prompt repetition with RoPE models
contributions.source_quote: We propose PTDO, a simple, training-free optimization that achieves the accuracy benefits of prompt repetition while halving the decode-time KV cache.

contributions.purpose: Empirically validate PTDO across models and benchmarks.
contributions.mechanism: Evaluate on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct across NameIndex (synthetic retrieval) and ARC-Challenge (options-first multiple choice), comparing Single P, Full P||P, and PTDO.
contributions.evaluation: 100%+ accuracy retention with ~50% KV reduction; e.g., Llama NameIndex 3.0% vs 2.8% (107% retention), ARC identical 73.5%; Qwen ARC 85.6% vs 85.5%; 49.4% KV cache reduction (193.2 MB vs 381.7 MB).
contributions.source_quote: We validate PTDO across two models (Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-7B) and two benchmarks (NameIndex, ARC-Challenge), demonstrating 100%+ accuracy retention with ~50% KV cache reduction.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Prompt repetition (Leviathan et al., 2025) is a simple yet effective technique that improves large language model (LLM) accuracy by duplicating the input prompt from P to P||P.
Unlike these general-purpose methods, PTDO exploits redundancy specific to prompt repetition—the first-copy KV cache is decode-time redundant—and is complementary to existing compression techniques.
Architectural modifications such as YOCO (Sun et al., 2024) redesign the decoder to cache keys and values only once.

PTDO fits naturally into this ecosystem as a simple, training-free optimization for prompt repetition scenarios that reduces decode-time memory without modifying attention computation or memory management.

notes: Decode throughput is essentially unchanged (~34-35 tok/s) and peak GPU memory is similar across conditions because the KV difference is negligible relative to model weights at batch size 1; the memory benefit is only realized at larger batch sizes or longer contexts. On several settings PTDO merely matches (not exceeds) full P||P, and total throughput is slightly lower than Single P.
